name: Ere
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only Ross 1988 comparative Admiralties data and a Kaipuleohone recording with printed notes; no grammar/phonology of Ere located.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian languages (revised edition). Asia-Pacific Linguistics Open Access Monographs. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Ere cited for low vowel dissimilation (*kanase > kinas, *mata-ña > mira-n), for prenasalised trills, and in ch. 9 syncope: 'in eastern Manus in the Admiralty Islands.. any unstressed vowel was deleted in the environment VC_CV.. Ere dralŋwa- ear.. Ere panna (with syncope and assimilation)'. Historical statement presupposing a stressed/unstressed contrast; no synchronic Ere stress rule.

sources.citation: Blevins, Juliette. 2007. Endangered sound patterns: three perspectives on theory and description. Language Documentation & Conservation 1(1):1-16.
sources.note: Mentions Ere only as a language with low vowel dissimilation (citing Blust 1996a,b); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record eree1241 (2 refs: Ross 1988, Blust 2007; 0 descriptive) and Wikipedia 'Ere language' (stub).
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; Wikipedia points only to the two Kaipuleohone items.

sources.note: Comparative-historical only; Ere appears solely in cognate sets and sound-correspondence tables (index: pp. 317-334). The five 'stress' hits in the whole book concern Schouten and Huon Gulf languages; nothing on Admiralties or Ere stress.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 1975 (Feb-Apr). Manus language packets: Ere' elicitation sheets (speaker Pompiran Kuyei, Loi village), pp. 34-55 of RB2-011, Robert Blust collection, Kaipuleohone, University of Hawai'i (unpublished handwritten field notes; low-res scans).
sources.note: All 22 Ere pages read visually. Stress is marked word by word with a raised tick before the stressed syllable (e.g. ru'woh 'two', tu'lah 'three', 'onah 'six', a'het, 'pandris, ka'ney, 'ilipep), with stress on initial, penultimate and final syllables all attested; marginal notes: p.34 '#57 In possessed like rear: kulŋam, -an | 1st syll stress'; p.42 (#438-439) 'either penult or final stress'; p.43 (#576) 'ilipep (Stress accepted on initial or final)'; p.50 analytical sheet: 'three /tulah/ -> [tu'lah] Stress final' and query list '7. Stress phonemic?'. No general rule is stated; p.51 is a conso…

Would settle whether stress is fixed or phonemic.
